title: Ekwe (box slit drum)
summary: The ekwe is a box of hardwood hollowed through a long slit. The two lips beside the slit are cut to different thickness, so one blow on the thick lip gives a deep knock and one on the thin lip a higher one.
howToPlay: Four places are lit: the Near lip, the Far lip, the Front of the box and the End.
Strike the place a closing ring marks. The near lip is deep, the far lip is high.
Keep the call steady: short and long strokes make the pattern.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: A slit drum carries a pattern of high and low strokes that stands for the tones of spoken words, so a skilled player can send a short message across a village.
credits: Tradition: the ekwe of the Igbo; patterns written for this game
